rv.q: Like Bruno’s insinuations, the power and compulsion of the play build slowly until you realise too late that you are altogether ensnared.
The whole show is an ingenious, grippingly nasty pleasure.
No Christmas ghost story will be quite as chilling (or gripping) as this nightmare.
The climax, entirely reimagined by Warner, is immensely powerful.
This ambitious, enjoyable attempt to turn Patricia Highsmith's novel into a fully fledged stage noir has a few flaws.
The problem is that what starts as fast-moving noirish narrative shifts uneasily into Freudian casebook.
But it never sucks you in emotionally, and for a thriller it just isn't very thrilling.
It could hardly be more impressive, but there is a hole at the centre.
Robert Allan Ackerman's production is stylish yet feels under-powered.
You should see this production just to marvel at the design work.
Craig Warner's adaptation of Patricia Highsmith's novel makes for a clumsy and clunky ride.

cn.t: A visually striking adaptation with spectacular set changes and cinematic noir style, but critics find the thriller lacks suspense and dramatic punch, resulting in mixed-to-negative reception.
